clue.text: Appropriate Republican probing American in high position

indicators.note: probing means poking into something, so the R goes inside the word for high

parts.note: up means raised or in a high position

explanation.surface: A Republican politician pokes into an American's lofty office in order to grab it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective, but here it is the verb meaning to seize; 'probing' names the insertion of the Republican's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to seize or take over without right, a synonym for usurping.

clue.text: Generous firm leaving barrister to seek information

indicators.note: leaving means departing from, so the letters for a firm are taken out

parts.note: counsel is a barrister arguing a case
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to fish is to seek information indirectly

explanation.surface: A company drops its lawyer to dig for facts generously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes CO from COUNSEL, giving UNSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Unselfish means putting others first, so giving freely and generous.

clue.text: Taking great interest is normally right for everyone

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the letter for right replaces the word for everyone

parts.note: usually means normally
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Being keenly interested is usually the right thing for all people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts R where ALL stood in USUALLY. 'great interest' looks like enthusiasm but means excessive money interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Usury is lending money at an exorbitant rate, the charging of excessive interest.

clue.text: Some nearly went astray in formal garden

parts.note: part means some of something

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: erred means went astray, did wrong

explanation.surface: Some visitors almost got lost in an ornamental garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops D from ERRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is a level garden laid out in formal ornamental beds.

clue.text: Old ruler warns what conspirators are

parts.note: an Inca was a ruler of the old Peruvian empire
hoots means sounds a horn, so warns other road users

explanation.surface: An ancient king cautions those plotting against him.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspirators are secretly working together, an idiom for being in league.

clue.text: Press Club

definitions.meaning: to press clothes with a hot appliance
a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for smoothing creased clothes and a metal-headed golf club.

clue.text: Highlights in obvious fabrication

parts.note: clear means obvious
a story is a made-up tale, a fabrication

explanation.surface: The main points of a plainly invented account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlights' reads as best bits, but means windows that let in light high up in a church wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearstory is the upper wall of a church nave pierced with windows, so a row of high lights.

clue.text: Sibyl, missing line, goes after hot poet

indicators.note: goes after means comes next, so the reworked oracle follows the H

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, on taps

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for line is taken out

parts.note: a sibyl was a prophetess, an oracle

explanation.surface: A prophetess, minus one line, pursues a passionate versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: A sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world, hence an oracle; 'missing' names the dropped line and 'goes after' places the result behind hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a leading Roman lyric poet of the Augustan age.

clue.text: Deliveries wasted, roses being so past their best

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries
blown means wasted, as money is blown

explanation.surface: Faded roses are like a spell of bowling thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a set of six balls bowled in cricket. 'roses being so' tells you the definition describes blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Overblown flowers are fully open and starting to fade, so beyond their prime.

clue.text: Column emitting metallic sound

indicators.note: sound means what is heard, so the word for metallic is said aloud

parts.note: steel is a metal, standing in for metallic

explanation.surface: A pillar gives off a clanging noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' turns STEEL, heard, into a word spelt differently; 'emitting' links the definition to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stele is an upright stone slab or pillar bearing an inscription.

clue.text: Dull individual back here after failure

parts.note: a square is a dull, conventional person; with the next word it reads 'dull individual'
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A boring person returns to this spot once things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull individual' reads as one phrase but splits: SQUARE (a dull, conventional sort) and ONE (an individual).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'back to the starting point' is used for having to begin again after a plan fails.

clue.text: Engineers have day before magistrate

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
eve is the day before a festival or event

explanation.surface: The Royal Engineers meet the judge the evening before.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official with judicial duties in medieval England, a historical sense of magistrate.

clue.text: Non-professionals treated meanly

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Amateurs were handled stingily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges MEANLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Laymen are people without professional or specialist training, the amateurs of a field.

clue.text: Miller's bewitching play it gets very heated

definitions.meaning: Arthur Miller's drama about the Salem witch trials
a vessel for melting metals at very high temperatures

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both Arthur Miller's witch-trial play and a heat-resistant pot used for melting metal.

clue.text: Assembly requiring father to hold post up

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the reversed post goes inside the word for father

parts.note: a father is a parent

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: mail is post, letters

explanation.surface: A gathering needs Dad to keep the mail raised.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read from bottom to top, so the post runs backwards; 'to hold' names the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is a legislative assembly of elected representatives.

clue.text: With various religions in it, father gets converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest who changes faith embraces many religions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets converted' rearranges IN IT and FATHER together; 'converted' also plays on religious conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Interfaith describes something involving people of several different faiths.

clue.text: Farewell horrid lepidoptera: none seen for ages!

indicators.note: horrid means nasty or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
seen for means appearing in place of, so the letter for none replaces the word for ages

parts.note: an era is an age, a long period
O is a zero, none

explanation.surface: Goodbye to nasty butterflies and moths: none have been seen for years!
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen for' puts O where ERA stood in LEPIDOPTERA, giving LEPIDOPTO, which 'horrid' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a jaunty, old-fashioned British slang word for goodbye.

clue.text: Not quite light enough for a necklace

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a torch is a portable light

explanation.surface: The lamp gives too little light to see a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter, H, from TORCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a twisted metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts, a kind of necklace.

clue.text: Gossip's beginning to concern milliner to the Queen

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is a gossip, a person

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a hatter makes and sells hats, like a milliner
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle starts to bother a hat-maker serving the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives C, the first letter of 'concern'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterer talks idly at length, a gossiping person.

clue.text: Tree planted in a garden plot enjoyed a soaking

indicators.note: planted in means set into, so the tree goes inside the other words

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden for flowers
a sorb is a tree, the service tree or rowan

explanation.surface: A tree set in a flowerbed revels in a good watering.
explanation.walkthrough: The sorb, or service tree, is a crossword regular; 'planted in' names the insertion, and the definition plays on a well-watered garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbed means soaked up liquid, the playful sense of taking in a soaking.

clue.text: Bear's coming back as children's toy

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Pooh is the bear of the children's stories; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A teddy bear returns as a child's plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns POOH into the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a large ring rolled along or spun round the waist by children, a plaything.

clue.text: Rose seen spilling fluid on bar

indicators.note: spilling means tipping out messily, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flower appears as someone knocks a drink over on a pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' rearranges FLUID ON BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A floribunda is a type of rose bearing dense clusters of flowers.

clue.text: Section of autopsy chosen for horror film

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a post-mortem is chosen for a scary movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for' into the definition; it is a link word, and the definition is just 'horror film', misread in the source as 'her rer film'.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller, a classic of the horror genre.

clue.text: One leaving pitch to fight for a mineral

indicators.note: leaving means going away from, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: a field is a sports pitch
I is the Roman numeral for one
to spar is to fight, as in boxing practice

explanation.surface: A player walks off the field to brawl over a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I out of FIELD, giving FELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Feldspar is a common rock-forming silicate, one of the most abundant minerals in the crust.

clue.text: Leader of Tories involved in payments for honours

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the letter goes into the word for payments

parts.note: fees are payments

indicators.note: Leader of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A party leader is mixed up in cash for honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of' gives T from 'Tories', which 'involved in' puts inside FEES.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to celebrate and honour them publicly.

clue.text: Australian resident wants bill cut back

indicators.note: back means in reverse, so the run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab
to mow is to cut grass

explanation.surface: Someone living in Australia wants his invoice reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TABMOW right round.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing marsupial native to Australia, so an inhabitant of that country.

clue.text: Piece of equipment that's new to Old Bill picked up?

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted from the bottom, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tab is a bill

explanation.surface: A truncheon is new kit for the British police to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Bill is British slang for the police, which makes this look like a police truncheon; in fact 'Old' and 'Bill' are separate. 'picked up' turns TAB into BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a stick carried as equipment, by a relay runner, conductor or policeman.

clue.text: Wielder of hammer, painfully sensitive, heard lisping?

indicators.note: heard lisping means spoken with an S turned into TH, so the word is said aloud with a lisp

parts.note: sore means painfully sensitive

explanation.surface: Someone swinging a hammer, hurting badly, speaks with a lisp.
explanation.walkthrough: SORE said with a lisp comes out as 'thore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse god of thunder who wields the hammer Mjolnir.

clue.text: Subject to choose shortly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shortly means in short form, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: Someone is required to make a choice soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops K from PICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject of discussion or writing.

clue.text: I hit boxer, terrible showman

indicators.note: terrible means awful or wild, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A boastful performer admits punching a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges I HIT BOXER.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibitor puts things on show, so is one who displays, a kind of showman.

clue.text: Imbibe one drink, then a second

parts.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer, one kind of drink

explanation.surface: Someone drinks one glass and then has another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a second' looks like a second drink, but it is the definition: a second attends a duellist or boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is the helper who backs a boxer or duellist, a backer.

clue.text: Benefactor has name inscribed in entrance

indicators.note: inscribed in means written into, so the letter goes inside the word for entrance

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A patron has his name carved over a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inscribed in' puts N inside DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods, a giver or benefactor.
